sentences.text: Revenue compounded 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].
Operating income grew faster at 9.9% a year, but net income grew only 0.4% and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year [F146][F147][F149].

FY2021 was the sharp break: operating margin fell 14.6pp to 15.5% as operating income dropped 43.1% [D107][F20][D97], with NEER's results held back by the absence of 2020's Spain project gain and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity [P63].
FY2023 reversed it, operating margin rising 23.5pp to 41.3% [D177][F22], helped by $1,729 million of non-qualifying hedge gains in NEER's net income [P30].
FY2025 net income slipped 1.6% to $6.84 billion [D238][F32] on lower Corporate and Other results, partly offset by higher FPL and NEER results [P24].
FPL remains the revenue base at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue, down from 76.5% in FY2020 [D271][D258].
FPL contributed 5.5pp of FY2025's 9.8% revenue growth [D273][D236], and its revenue rose $1.24 billion on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues [P21].
NEER's segment net income rose to $2,975 million in FY2025 [S29], reflecting higher earnings from new investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Operating income grew 10.7% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D237][D236], an incremental margin of 34.8% [D256].
Diluted EPS fell 2.1% while net income fell 1.6% [D240][D238], as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D251].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high and far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D300][D299][D298].
The FY2025 margin was essentially flat, up 0.3pp [D247], as operating expenses grew 10.0% against 9.8% revenue growth [D249][D236].
Depreciation and amortization rose $951 million, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs of about $1,090 million tied to Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [P16].

Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% [D248][F40] even as operating margin held, because other income (expense) was -$3,750 million [X64] on unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances [P8].
The effective tax rate of -17.7% [D226] reflects clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million in 2025 [P11].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][D227], in line with the 1.55x to 2.73x range of recent years [D157][D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241] as the change from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Investing cash outflow of $23.9 billion [F72] dwarfs operating cash flow, and D&A of $6.58 billion equals 25.5% of revenue [X32][D224], reflecting the capital-intensive build.
Stock-based compensation is small at 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so it does not distort conversion.
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231], with total debt of $95.0 billion [D230] against cash of $2.81 billion [F96].
Long-term debt grew 18.8% a year over the window [F156], and net cash as a share of revenue ranks at the 0th percentile against four utilities peers, whose median is -228.4% [D314][D315].
The current ratio of 0.60x is the window high but still below 1.0x [F128][D305], and working capital is -$9.23 billion [F120].
Free cash flow is negative, so capital return of $4.68 billion in dividends [D233] was funded alongside $23.4 billion of debt issued [X90], and the diluted share count still rose 0.6% [D251].
Net cash fell for a seventh straight year, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025 [R2][D9][D231], a structural feature of the regulated and renewable build rather than a one-off.
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025 [R1][F128], so short-term liabilities exceed current assets by $9.23 billion [F120].
FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% [D201][R3], which the filing attributes to lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues [P35].
The effective tax rate swung -23.3pp to -17.7% in FY2025 [R4][D226], driven by clean energy tax credits [P11], which makes the net margin harder to read.
FY2019 operating expenses were later restated to $14,257 million from $13,851 million [R5][X18], a data-quality caveat on that year's margin.
Operating margin: a print below the 30.3% window median [D300] in the FY2026 10-K would signal the FY2023 hedge-driven peak is unwinding.
Net cash: further deterioration beyond -$92.2 billion [D231] would extend the seven-year trend and pressure the balance sheet.
Operating cash flow conversion: a ratio below the 1.55x FY2023 low [D157] would flag working-capital strain from cost recovery clauses.
